chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the inheritances: what Islam acquired from the wealth of the Polytheists which had not been distributed, then for the women are their shares from it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheriting unallocated wealth from polytheists in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (as) judicial application of inheritance laws to the *Fay'* or unallocated war booty acquired during the early Islamic period, specifically addressing the status of polytheists' wealth. It underscores the principle that even in the context of communal state assets (*Māl al-Mushrikīn*), the fixed shares (*Huẓū*) of female heirs are preserved and distributed according to Sharia, reflecting the comprehensive nature of Ali’s legal reasoning.
